warnings: Reframe: move camera closer and/or zoom so the window and impact point dominate; remove/reposition the large dark foreground obstruction.
Stage the brick: increase size/readability, ensure it’s clearly red clay, and place it on a strong left→right path through the pane center; add motion blur.

Shatter dynamics: increase fracture density and vary shard sizes (large primary shards near impact, smaller secondary fragments outward); increase outward velocities so shards travel into camera space.
Add a crack pass: emphasize radial + concentric cracking before breakup so the remaining pane reads as stressed/partially attached and collapsing.
Lighting: add a motivated key + rim/specular lights aimed to catch shard edges; raise exposure ~0.7–1.5 stops while keeping a night mood.
Material work: build convincing rusted steel and aged concrete (roughness variation, grime, stains, chipped paint).
Glass shader: strengthen specular/edge highlights, ensure believable thickness/IOR; reduce “flat” look so shards sparkle when lit.
Render quality: increase samples and/or denoise more carefully to remove under-sampled grain without smearing shard detail.

Script parameter targets (shader microdetail): try reducing Line 129 bump Distance (0.15 → ~0.03–0.08) to avoid blobby surface distortion; adjust Line 203 voronoi Scale (15.0 → ~25–45) to increase perceived crack cell density; reduce overly strong wave distortion (Line 314 Distortion 6.0 → ~1–3) if it’s warping the glass read; lower Line 331 bump Strength (0.12 → ~0.04–0.08) if highlights are breaking up unnaturally.
